summary: PowerShell example creating a self-signed certificate, an HTTPS WinRM listener on port 5986, and a firewall rule, with a warning that the scripts are for demonstration and need review before production use.
questions: How do I add an HTTPS WinRM listener with a self-signed cert?
What port does WinRM over HTTPS use?
Is the sample WinRM setup script safe for production?

answer_card.title: Adding an HTTPS WinRM listener
answer_card.answer_md:
```powershell
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -CertStoreLocation 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My' -DnsName $env:COMPUTERNAME -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddYears(1) -Provider 'Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider' -Subject "CN=$env:COMPUTERNAME"

New-Item -Path 'WSMan:\localhost\Listener' -Address '*' -CertificateThumbprint $cert.Thumbprint -Enabled $true -Port 5986 -Transport HTTPS -Force

New-NetFirewallRule -Action Allow -Direction Inbound -DisplayName 'Windows Remote Management (HTTPS-In)' -LocalPort 5986 -Profile Any -Protocol TCP
```

These are demo scripts: review them before production, since opening the port to all, local-account access, and self-signed certs may not suit your environment.
